application.name: Color Convert
application.description: A synthetic camera's NV12 or YUYV frames converted to RGBA by holoscan-color-convert's ColorConvertOp and letterboxed by its ResizeOp in the same pass, with the camera's info from a camera_info file resized alongside, shown by HoloViz in a window or rendered offscreen, with every output, resized camera info and render checked against the module's CPU reference on one worker.

changelog.1.0.0: Initial release: the holoscan-color-convert demo, with a synthetic NV12/YUYV camera, ColorConvertOp and ResizeOp on the cuda, vic or auto backend, a HoloViz window or offscreen render, and checks against the CPU reference.

hardware.name: NVIDIA GPU
hardware.description: A CUDA-capable GPU supported by the Holoscan SDK.

hardware.name: Display
hardware.description: For the window mode only; the offscreen and ci modes need none.

window.description: Live: 1920x1080 NV12 at 30 frames per second, converted to RGBA and shown in a HoloViz window with the 640x640 letterboxed resize inset, until the window is closed.

offscreen.description: HoloViz renders offscreen into CUDA memory: 60 frames on one worker, each output and resized camera info checked against the CPU reference and each render against its frame.

ci.description: Finite headless check on one worker: 60 YUYV and 1080p frames on the auto backend, every output checked against the CPU reference (byte for byte on CUDA, within tolerance on the VIC) and every resized camera info against the resized camera; on a CI runner, auto must take the VIC on the Jetson and CUDA on x86_64.
